newsitem.title: USA: Uncooperative juror forces delay in Food Lion trial.
newsitem.headline: Uncooperative juror forces delay in Food Lion trial.

text.p: An uncooperative juror forced a delay Wednesday in a civil jury's deliberations over whether the ABC television netowrk must pay punitive damages to Food Lion Inc.
After deliberating four hours Wednesday, the jury sent the judge a note indicating that one of the 12 jurors was not cooperating and asked how to proceed.

"We have one juror who refuses to negotiate on proposed figures that 11 others are willing to consider," the jury's note read. "It has become very troublesome. This juror has taken a personal side to this trial, not based on evidence and documentation and instructions. This juror seems to have their mind made up prior to negotiations and unwilling to work with the other jurors. Please advise."
U.S. District Judge Carlton Tilley, repeating jury instructions he had given Tuesday, told the reassembled jurors to recall their oath to deliberate in good faith.

"It is your duty as jurors to discuss the case with one another in an effort to reach agreement if you can do so. Each of you must decide the case for yourself, but only after full consideration of the evidence with the other members of the jury," he said.
The decision to order punitive damages must be unanimous.

Food Lion sued ABC, owned by Walt Disney Co., and four producers over a hidden camera investigation of its stores in the Carolinas in 1992. The report, which aired on ABC's PrimeTime Live programme, charged Food Lion sold old meat and fish and used unsanitary food handling practices.
Food Lion, based in Salisbury, N.C., is a unit of Belgian retailer Ets Delhaize Freres et Cie "LE LION' SA and had 1996 sales of $9 billion.

Tilley instructed the jury of six men and six women to make its decision based only the evidence, follow the law as he instructed, and not be influenced by sympathy or prejudice for either party. The jury resumed deliberations late Wednesday afternoon.
